text: COMPUTATIONAL SCIENCE · A SOURCE-LINKED INDEX Gordon Bell Prize Paper Archive An archive centered on finalist and prize-winning papers, with historical competition entries in a separate index. Some entries are not confirmed finalists or single papers. The work behind the performance. Explore the teams and machines behind these records, and what their performance numbers actually measure. HISTORICAL INDEX Annual sources and DOI records first · manuscript checks shown separately —years represented in the index —annual candidate entries —entries with verified DOIs —papers with manuscript details The first three figures describe the annual candidate index. Manuscript details cover a selected subset and are not added to the indexed-entry total. Coverage varies by year; a verified DOI does not mean that its manuscript or performance has been audited. Web rosters and local copies have separate audit states. SC26 has a dated postconference review of program membership, award evidence, publisher bylines and DOI resolution; conference-day final scores remain unverified. Annual links come from the official SC history directory; original websites are linked where listed, with proceedings and history PDFs as other entry points. HDD-origin copy receipts (86 records) This is the original copy inventory from 12 November 2026. It records titles, source files and verified hashes from the connected HDD. Current manuscript availability and scientific review are shown in the collection summary and each year above; the receipt inventory is not the current collection total. Manuscripts remain private. One candidate, a result history Submitted manuscripts, revised papers, conference talks and official updates remain separate evidence stages. A later score does not erase the earlier paper result. Revision, measurement, presentation and checking dates are distinct. Unknown is a useful result A machine’s advertised capacity is not an application result. Missing precision and missing throughput are labelled explicitly. These records are not a performance ranking. Sources at the field level Selection, award result, bibliography, abstract and measurements link to their own evidence.
